traits.wood_density_basic_kg_m3.note: GWDD v.2.2 species aggregate for Carnegiea gigantea (gwddagg_v2.2_species.csv, read): specific gravity 0.34 (wsg_est, the database's hierarchical-model species mean, from 1 record in 1 source); trunks 0.34, branches 0.4. Basic density (oven-dry mass over green volume) is the specific gravity times 1000 kg/m3.

traits.juvenile_period_years.note: FEIS (Helmy 2021, read): most saguaros begin producing fruit when about 2 to 2.5 m tall, about 30 to 50 years old. The Woody Plant Seed Manual (Carnegiea, read): reproductive maturity at about 2 m and an age of about 40 years (Steenbergh and Lowe 1983). The succulent program's own bloom_age, scaled by vigour, stays; the period is for the checks.

traits.note: Britton and Rose's The Cactaceae (vol. 2, 1920, p. 164): stems and branches 30 to 65 cm thick, with 12 to 24 blunt ribs 1 to 3 cm high; areoles about 2.3 cm apart (the scan's digit is unsure), nearly touching near the top, densely brown-felted; the central spines stouter than the radials, often 7 cm long. Spine counts are not given.

traits.areole_spacing_m.note: FEIS's saguaro review (Helmy 2021): areoles 1.2 to 3 cm apart along the ribs; the usual spacing is Britton and Rose's 2.3 cm.

generator.params.note: Hand-set from general knowledge of the species: a single ribbed column that grows a few centimetres in its first decade and fastest in middle age, to 12 to 15 m in about two centuries; its tip widens to an adult diameter near 50 cm, so juveniles are club-shaped. Arms come late (after about 65 years and 3 m), from the middle of the trunk, nearly level, turning up at a constricted elbow; a few droop after freezes. White flowers ring the tips of trunk and arms in late spring with buds and red fruit. Not fitted to measurements.

allometry.note: Rough heights from general knowledge of saguaro growth at sites like Saguaro National Park: about a metre by 40 years, a few metres by 80, about seven by 125. Wide tolerances; replace with measured growth curves before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: Colours chosen by eye from photographs: a dull grey-green skin with darker pleats, 12 to 24 ribs by girth, areoles about 2.5 cm apart with brown felt, a dozen or more short radial spines and a few longer, darker centrals, the lowest pointing down, greying with age; old plants corky at the base. Waxy white flowers with yellow centres. Its flower, bud and fruit are drawn from its characters by the rules at Cactaceae and the flowering plants: tepals on a spiral, as many and as broad as the family's rules give, on a floral cup above the inferior ovary, its stamens, style and stigma lobes, and its fruit from its stated colour, size and surface. Until 2026-10-18 its flower and fruit looks were partly set by hand (round tepal tips, a centre and an accent colour by eye), and a look set by hand keeps the rule that gives it the year its months state from running, so it flowered and fruited all year.

traits.flowering_months.note: USA-NPN Nature's Notebook phenometrics (getSummarizedData, fetched 2026-10-18; the phenology method of 2026-10-14: each individual-year span of the phenophase counted day by day, keeping the months with at least a third of the busiest month's days), Carnegiea gigantea (species 210): 806 open-flower spans on 77 sites, by far most days in May (5,886), then June (1,800) and April (796); April to June kept, as the model estimate it replaces had them. Anderson (The Cactus Family p. 139) gives late spring.

traits.stigma_colour.note: Flora of North America vol. 4 (read on eFloras 2026-10-18), Carnegiea: stigma lobes about 10, tannish white; a warm off-white by hand.
